sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The HASH_JOIN (node 8) processes ~99K filtered trips rows with a per-row CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) against only 265 zones rows, making the join build/probe and the cast the dominant CPU cost.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

The CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) in the join condition forces a per-row conversion on the 99K-row trips side; if PULocationID is already a compatible integer type, removing the cast would eliminate this CPU overhead.

The RIGHT HASH_JOIN builds a hash table on the 99K filtered trips rows instead of the 265-row zones table; reversing the build/probe order (e.g., by rewriting as LEFT JOIN or hinting) would reduce hash memory and probe time.

The SEQ_SCAN on trips reads all row groups despite only needing PULocationID and payment_type; if the table is partitioned or has zone maps on payment_type, predicate pushdown could skip irrelevant row groups and reduce I/O.
